    "summary": "Inspired by the cuisines and communities of New York City, Tatiana makes fine dining feel fun again.",

    {
      "title": "NYC’s Longest Restaurant Lines, Ranked",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/nyc-restaurant-lines",
      "position": 4,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Our highest-rated restaurant has a predictable line that’s also semi-sheltered by the Lincoln Center architecture. Just show up at by 4:30pm and you’ll usually get a bar seat, and if it’s cold, a hot beverage while you wait for the doors to open. If you're with a group and get a later table, duck in to the Lobby Bar at David Geffen Hall, drink a glass of wine, and send a few emails (there’s wifi)."
    },
    {
      "title": "Restaurants Where You Should Read The Dessert Menu First",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/restaurants-with-great-dessert-nyc",
      "position": 10,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Our [top-rated restaurant](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurants-nyc), this excellent Lincoln Center spot serves food inspired by the chef’s roots in the Bronx and beyond. Their Bodega Special is an instant NYC classic. It’s a nostalgic reimagining of two iconic after-school treats, the kind you couldn’t tear the plastic wrapping off fast enough: a fudgy cosmic brownie, complete with rainbow sprinkles, and ice cream that tastes uncannily like a powdered sugar donut. Move over, Little Debbie."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Outdoor Dining In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurant-patios-nyc",
      "position": 11,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Reservations at Tatiana are nearly impossible. The good news? Their outdoor dining, on a patio in Lincoln Center, is walk-in-only, making it by far the easiest way to try their pastrami suya. Yeah, you’ll be missing out on the quasi-nightclub vibes of the dining room. But eating curried goat patties and short rib pastrami suya with a breeze in the sunshine is a reasonable consolation."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Best Restaurants For Special Occasions In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/special-occasion-date-night-restaurants",
      "position": 12,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "The food at Tatiana is excellent, but it’s the party vibe of this Lincoln Center restaurant that makes it a top choice for an occasion when you want to wear something sparkly, dig into several meaty dishes, and possibly do a jello shot along the way. Getting a reservation for a group is almost impossible, but parties of two can snag walk-in seats at the bar. You’ll have to get in line for those, which is a great way to score brownie points with whoever you’re dining with. Once you’re in, start with the crisp curried goat patties and some crab rangoon."
    },
    {
      "title": "The Toughest Reservations In NYC Right Now (And How To Get Them)",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/toughest-restaurant-reservations-nyc",
      "position": 20,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "**Verdict:** Simply put: one of the [best restaurants](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurants-nyc) in NYC. Located inside David Geffen Hall on the [Upper West Side](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/upper-west-side-restaurants), Tatiana feels like a quiet nightclub—with soft blue lighting and beaded silver curtains—and serves food that blends Afro-Caribbean flavors with iconic New York dishes. Options include braised oxtails, curried goat patties, and excellent short rib pastrami suya."
    },
    {
      "title": "Top 25: The Best Restaurants In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurants-nyc",
      "position": 18,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Like a ’90s nightclub plopped into the middle of Lincoln Center, Tatiana glows blue and chain-link gold, blasts Lauryn Hill and Biggie, and turns the whole concept of an extravagant Manhattan evening into something that involves tearing open curried goat patties and licking sticky oxtail juice off your fingers. You’ll have just as much fun clocking tracks on the throwback playlist as you will dissecting all the menu’s references to NYC classics, from Afro-Caribbean hot bars to Chinese takeout. You’ll even find a nod to the Cosmic brownies at corner bodegas. We're especially fond of the absurdly tender short rib pastrami suya, served with caraway coco bread—an invitation to build your own slider. Tatiana is one of the [hardest reservations](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/toughest-restaurant-reservations-nyc) in town, but for a restaurant that feels like a paradigm shift in New York fine dining, it’s worth it."
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Eat & Drink Before (& After) Seeing A Broadway Show, According To JoJo",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/theater-district-restaurant-guide-broadway-jojo",
      "position": 1,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "“This place is absolutely magical and inspiring. It was just a very sensuous experience at Lincoln Center. We ate the egusi dumplings with a Nigerian red stew and Jonah crab. And, excuse me, the large plate of braised oxtails with a thumbelina carrot and a chayote squash. The short rib, the pastrami suya, and the Mom Duke’s shrimp—everything was off the chain. It's amazing. [Kwame] is so talented.”"
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Eat Near Columbus Circle",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/columbus-circle-restaurants",
      "position": 2,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Tatiana is the [best restaurant](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurants-nyc) in New York City, and it comes from Kwame Onwuachi. You might know of him from his DC restaurants or his run on _Top Chef_, but he’s also the guy who single-handedly made Lincoln Center cool again. Tatiana, located inside David Geffen Hall (the one with the Philharmonic) feels like a quiet nightclub and serves food that blends Afro-Caribbean flavors with iconic New York dishes. Think: egusi dumplings and curried goat patties, and wagyu pastrami suya—a must order."
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Go When You Can't Get Into Masalawala & Sons",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/where-to-go-when-you-cant-get-into-masalawala-and-sons",
      "position": 2,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Kwame Onwuachi (_Top Chef_ and _Selena + Chef_) has returned to NYC to open this restaurant in the renovated David Geffen Hall at Lincoln Center. Much like Masalawala is inspired by the food in Kolkata (the owner’s hometown), Tatiana is heavily influenced by Onwuache’s upbringing in the Bronx. It feels like a quiet nightclub here, and the menu blends Afro-Caribbean flavors with iconic New York dishes—think egusi dumplings and a mizuna caesar salad with Trini green seasoning. The must-order here is the Wagyu short rib pastrami suya. Reservations for Tatiana are also tough to get, but your best chance is finding a table for a late dinner or for the same day if you check the morning of."
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Hang Out Near 14 Restaurants With Long Waits",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/restaurants-with-long-waits-nyc-nearby-bars",
      "position": 1,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "**The Waiting Room: **[The Lobby Bar](https://lincolncenter.org/venue/david-geffen-hall/info/the-lobby-bar-menu) at David Geffen Hall** **\n\n**The Back-Up Plan: **[Rampoldi](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/rampoldi)\n\nIf you show up at Lincoln Center by 4:30pm on a weekday, you might actually get a bar seat at Tatiana, one of the city's [best restaurants](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-restaurants-nyc), at 5pm. But it you can't make that happen, put your name in, make peace with your wait, and then do one of two things. If it’s before 8pm, go across the vestibule to the [Lobby Bar](https://lincolncenter.org/venue/david-geffen-hall/info/the-lobby-bar-menu) at David Geffen Hall, where you can get a glass of wine and send a few last-minute emails (there’s wifi in there). Or, head across the street to [Rampoldi](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/rampoldi). The Monte Carlo import has a long bar that's never too crowded, and if you want to start big spending, you can get a $45 martini with gold flakes."
    }
  ]
}

      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Everything at Don Angie is a little different, from the cheese-covered chrysanthemum salad and large-format lasagna for two, to the cocktail with prosciutto-washed rum and the notably large bathroom with a heavy sliding door that’s somewhat hard to lock.       "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/the-best-restaurants-in-the-west-village",

      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Instead of cacio e pepe and carbonara, Don Angie does a giant platter of rolled lasagna for two and a plate of gnocchi with provolone. Both dishes are very much worth your time, and there are some other creative pastas and little plates that belong on your table too, like a stuffed garlic flatbread and a parmesan-covered chrysanthemum salad. Eat all of those things, and you’ll realize why this is one of the top Italian restaurants in NYC. The restaurant is filled with leather and shiny things, so it’s a sleek destination for a [date night](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-date-night-restaurants-nyc). (And so is [San Sabino](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/san-sabino), a seafood-centric spot from the same team, right around the corner.)"
    },
    {

      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Here’s an idea: Ditch work a little early and put your name in at Don Angie at 5pm. You can also make a reservation up to a week in advance through their [website](https://www.donangie.com/)."

    {
      "title": "Where To Go When You Can’t Get Into Carbone",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/restaurants-like-carbone-nyc",
      "position": 10,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Like Carbone, Don Angie is an Italian restaurant, but it’s less of a red-sauce place.     {
      "title": "Where To Go When You Can’t Get Into Lilia",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/italian-restaurants-like-lilia-nyc",
      "position": 2,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Don Angie is almost as difficult to get into as Lilia, and you probably won't find any reservations online—but it isn't impossible to get a bar seat at this West Village Italian restaurant. Just stop by and put your name on the waitlist. You might have to wait an hour and a half before you can eat your poppyseed-covered gnocchi and stuffed garlic flatbread, but there are plenty of [bars in the neighborhood](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-west-village-bars) where you can hang out and kill time."
    },
    {
      "title": "Where To Hang Out Near 14 Restaurants With Long Waits",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/restaurants-with-long-waits-nyc-nearby-bars",
      "position": 5,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "**The Waiting Room:** [The Happiest Hour](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/the-happiest-hour)\n\n**The Back-Up Plan:** [Tivoli Trattoria](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/tivoli-trattoria)\n\n[Don Angie](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/don-angie) and sister restaurant [San Sabino](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/san-sabino) are directly next to each other in the West Village, and in our wildest dreams, if we aren’t able to get into one, we just opt for the other. In reality, your best bet is [The Happiest Hour](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/the-happiest-hour), which can get a little crowded, but where you can drink a large format cocktail standing up, if need be. Or drink an Aperol spritz at [Tivoli Trattoria](https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/reviews/tivoli-trattoria)—it’s technically a restaurant, but it’s easy to get into, and it serves Italian food in case you get too hungry to wait for your table at Don Angie."

      "position": 1,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "**Perfect For:** Dinner\n\nMaybe a few people in your family don’t typically get along, and you’re afraid that someone will pick a fight with someone else, mostly out of boredom. Order both of those things, in addition to the stuffed garlic flatbread, and people should be too distracted to get overly passive aggressive."
    }

      "blurb": "It’s kind of a travesty that this place on the LES is known more for a fake orgasm scene than for the sliced meats behind their deli counter.     },
    {
      "title": "11 NYC Restaurants With Takeout Passover Specials",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/11-nyc-restaurants-with-takeout-passover-specials",
      "position": 9,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "Katz’s makes great matzo ball soup all year, and getting their Passover meal is a good excuse to reunite with it - while also eating honey layer cake and brisket. The famous Houston Street deli has [nationwide shipping available](https://katzsdelicatessen.com/) in case you want to send someone you love a seder in-a-box, as well as [Passover packages available for pick-up and delivery for $33.45 per person](https://localmenu.katzsdelicatessen.com/menu-and-local/passover.html). Each pick-up and delivery order comes with your choice of starter, main, and dessert, or you can order a la carte items like a seder plate or mini stuffed cabbages."
    },
    {
      "title": "13 Really Good Hot Dogs In NYC",
      "url": "https://www.theinfatuation.com/new-york/guides/best-hot-dogs-nyc",
      "position": 4,
      "entry_name": null,
      "blurb": "There are multiple pastrami counters at Katz’s, and they always have long lines. But if you look in the corner opposite the entrance, you’ll see a grill station where you can just walk up and grab a hot dog. The frankfurters here are all-beef and kosher, with natural casing that makes them nice and snappy, and you can get one for about $5. That’s a fifth of the price of a Katz’s pastrami sandwich, so if you recently gave all money to your landlord, consider going this route. Sauerkraut is optional, but highly recommended."
    },
